units.text: Child, choose instruction from your youth, and until your hair is gray you will find wisdom.
Approach her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits. For you will labor a little in her cultivation and soon eat from her produce.
How very harsh she is to the uninstructed! The fainthearted will not remain with her.
She will be upon him like a heavy testing stone, and he will not delay throwing her away.
For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
Listen, child, and receive my judgment; do not reject my counsel.
Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.
Place your shoulder beneath her and carry her, and do not resent her bonds.
Approach her with all your soul, and keep her ways with your whole strength.
Trace her out and seek her, and she will become known to you; when you have gained hold of her, do not let her go.
For in the end you will find her rest, and she will turn to gladness for you.
Her fetters will become a strong shelter for you, and her collars a robe of glory.
Every living creature loves its like, and every person his neighbor.
All flesh gathers according to kind, and a man will cling to someone like himself.
What fellowship can a wolf have with a lamb? So it is with a sinner and a godly person.
Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
Do not be much involved with another woman, nor be held in the arms of one who is not your own.
to preserve you from a married woman and from an alien tongue’s slander.
Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
For a prostitute’s price is as much as one loaf, but a woman hunts men’s precious lives.
Likewise, wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they may be won without a word through the conduct of their wives,
when they observe your pure conduct in fear.
Let your adornment not be the outward kind—braiding hair, putting on gold ornaments, or dressing in garments—
but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
The one who reveals secrets has destroyed trust and will certainly not find a friend close to his soul.
Love a friend and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, do not pursue him afterward.
But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized him and began choking him, saying, ‘Repay whatever you owe.’
So his fellow slave fell down and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Be patient with me, and I will repay you.’
But he was unwilling. Instead, he went and threw him into prison until he repaid what was owed.
When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were exceedingly grieved. They came and explained to their master everything that had happened.
Then his master summoned him and said, ‘Evil slave! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?’
His master became angry and handed him over to the torturers until he repaid everything owed.
So also My heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother from your hearts.”
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts great things. Look how small a fire sets so great a forest ablaze!
And the tongue is a fire. The tongue is established among our members as a world of unrighteousness, staining the whole body, setting the wheel of life ablaze, and itself set ablaze by Gehenna.
For every kind of wild animal and bird, of creeping creature and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind;
but no human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.
Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
Let a person examine himself, and in this way let him eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
For the one who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment upon himself.
For this reason many among you are weak and ill, and a considerable number are asleep.
But if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.
Yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we may not be condemned with the world.
Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you may not come together for judgment. I will arrange the remaining matters when I come.
Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this city, spend a year there, trade, and make a profit”—
you who do not know what tomorrow brings. What is your life? For you are a vapor, appearing for a little while and then disappearing.
Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we shall both live and do this or that.”
But now you boast in your pretensions. All such boasting is evil.
Therefore, although I have great boldness in Christ to command you to do what is fitting,
I appeal instead because of love, being as I am, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus—
I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while in chains,
who was once useless to you, but is now useful both to you and to me.
I have sent him back to you—him, that is, my very heart.
I wanted to keep him with me, so that in your place he might serve me in my chains for the gospel.
But without your consent I did not want to do anything, so that your good deed might be voluntary, rather than as though compelled.
For perhaps he was separated from you for a little while for this reason: that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
And if he has wronged you in anything, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel upon the oracle-piece of judgment, upon his breast, when he enters into the sanctuary, as a memorial before God.

And you shall set the braided ornaments upon the oracle-piece of judgment; you shall set the chains upon both sides of the oracle-piece, and the two rosettes upon both shoulders of the shoulder-piece in front.

And you shall set Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece of judgment; and it shall be upon Aaron’s breast when he enters into the sanctuary before the Lord. And Aaron shall bear the judgments of the sons of Israel upon his breast before the Lord continually.
Slaves, obey your masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as you would Christ,
not serving only when their eyes are on you, as people-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the soul,
serving with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to human beings,
knowing that whatever good each one does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether slave or free.
And masters, act in the same way toward them, giving up threats, knowing that both their Master and yours is in the heavens, and there is no partiality with Him.
Slaves, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh, not serving only when their eyes are on you, as people-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
Whatever you do, work from the soul, as for the Lord and not for human beings,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. You serve the Lord Christ.
For the one who does wrong will receive back the wrong he did, and there is no partiality.
Masters, provide your slaves with what is just and equitable, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.
But refuse younger widows, for when their desires turn them against Christ, they want to marry,
incurring judgment because they set aside their first faith.
And at the same time they learn to be idle, going around the houses, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they ought not to say.
Therefore I want younger women to marry, bear children, manage a household, and give the opponent no opportunity for abuse.
When David’s days drew near for him to die, he commanded his son Solomon, saying,
“I myself am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and be a man,

and keep the charge of the Lord your God: walk in His ways, keeping His commandments, statutes, and judgments written in Moses’ law, so that you may understand what you will do in everything that I command you,

so that the Lord may establish His word which He spoke, saying, ‘If your sons guard their way, walking before Me in truth with all their heart and all their soul,’ saying, ‘A man shall not be cut off for you from Israel’s throne.’

You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s forces, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, setting the blood of war in peace, and put innocent blood on the belt around his waist and the sandal on his foot.
Act according to your wisdom, and do not bring his gray hair down to Hades in peace.
Show mercy to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they came near to me in this way when I fled from your brother Absalom.

Behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera, a son of the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a painful curse on the day I went to Camps. He came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, ‘I will not put you to death with the sword.’
You must certainly not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You will know what to do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to Hades with blood.”
Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will greatly delight in His commandments.
His seed will be powerful in the land; a generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness remains for an age of an age.
Light sprang up in darkness for the upright— merciful, compassionate and righteous.
Kind is the man who has compassion and lends; he will manage his words with judgment.
Yet these were men of mercy, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten.
It will remain with their offspring; their descendants are a good inheritance.
Their offspring stood within the covenants, and their children did so because of them.
Their offspring will remain for ever, and their glory will not be blotted out.
Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name lives through generations.
Peoples will recount their wisdom, and the assembly proclaims their praise.
I too, the last, kept watch like someone gleaning behind grape-gatherers.
By the Lord’s blessing I came in time, and like a grape-gatherer I filled a winepress.
Consider that I have labored not for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite replied: “I am younger in time, and you are older; therefore I kept quiet, afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.
I said, ‘Time is what speaks, and in many years people know wisdom.’
But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.
Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will announce to you what I know.’
How great is the multitude of Thy kindness, Lord, which Thou didst conceal for those who fear Thee, which Thou didst accomplish for those who hope in Thee before the sons of men!
Thou wilt hide them in the hiding place of Thy presence from human turmoil; Thou wilt shelter them in a tent from the contradiction of tongues.
David lamented this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
and he gave orders to teach the sons of Judah—behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright—
“Set up a memorial, Israel, for the dead, slain upon your heights! How the mighty have fallen!
Do not report it in Gath, and do not proclaim good news in Ashkelon’s exits, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
Mountains in Gilboa, let no dew descend and no rain upon you, nor fields of firstfruits! For there the shield of the mighty was treated with contempt; Saul’s shield was not anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow did not turn back empty, and Saul’s sword did not return empty.
Saul and Jonathan, loved and beautiful, not separated, splendid in their life and not separated in their death: swifter than eagles, they proved stronger than lions.
Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with your adornment, who put gold adornment upon your clothing.
How the mighty have fallen in the midst of war! Jonathan lies slain upon your heights.
I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan. You were very beautiful to me; your love for me was wonderful, beyond the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the equipment of war has perished!”
He waters mountains from His upper chambers; the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.
He makes grass spring up for livestock and green plants for the service of humans, to bring bread out of the earth;
and wine gladdens the human heart, to brighten the face with oil, and bread makes the human heart firm.
For the Lord had not given her a child, in her affliction and in the despondency of her affliction. She was despondent because of this: the Lord had shut her womb so as not to give her a child.
He would do this year after year when she went up to the Lord’s house, and she would be despondent and weep and not eat.
Thus says the Lord: “Because Zion’s daughters were exalted and walked with high neck and glancing eyes, dragging their tunics as their feet moved and playing with their feet,
You will return in your God; keep mercy and judgment, and draw near to your God continually.

and they will rejoice greatly in the Lord.” Let my soul exult in the Lord, for He clothed me in a garment of salvation and a tunic of joy. Like a bridegroom He placed a turban on me, and like a bride He adorned me with ornaments.
An evil person does evil things with insolence, but those who understand themselves are wise.
withdraw backward; do not show contempt,
lest the friend reproach you, and your battle and enmity not depart, but be for you equal to death.
withdraw backward; do not show contempt,
lest the friend reproach you, and your battle and enmity not depart, but be for you equal to death.
An evil person does harm when he mixes with a righteous person, and he hates the sound of security.
Thou wilt release my soul from my breath, and my bones from death.
For I will not live for ever, so as to keep enduring; leave me alone, for my life is empty.
A gentle-tempered man is a physician of the heart, but a perceptive heart is a moth to the bones.
Do not dine with a begrudging man, and do not desire his foods,
for as if someone swallowed a hair, so he eats and drinks.
Do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him, for he will vomit it and ruin your good words.
One who lives extravagantly from childhood will become a household servant, and in the end he will grieve over himself.
Do not give yourself as a pledge out of deference to a face.
For if you have no means from which to pay, they will take the bedding from beneath your sides.

a person to whom God will give wealth, possessions and glory, so that his soul lacks nothing it desires, yet God will not empower him to eat from it, for a stranger will eat it. This is futility and a grievous sickness.

units.text: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever tears down a fence will be bitten by a snake.
Whoever lifts stones will be worn out by them; whoever splits wood will be endangered by it.
If the iron falls out and he has troubled the face, he will strengthen his forces; and wisdom is the advantage of the courageous man.
If the snake bites without a whispered charm, there is no advantage for the charmer.
As healers put forward words to people, and the first to meet the word will be tripped up,
so are all who ambush their own friends, and when detected say, “I did it in play.”
With much wood a fire flourishes, but where there is no double-minded person, battle is quiet.
A hearth for coals and wood for fire, and an abusive man for the turmoil of battle.
The words of tricksters are soft, but they strike into the store-chambers of the inward parts.
Silver given with deceit must be regarded like a potsherd; smooth lips cover a painful heart.
A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
A foolish man digs evils for himself, and upon his own lips stores up fire.
A crooked man sends out evils, lights a torch of deceit for evil people, and separates friends.
A lawless man puts friends to the test, and leads them away into ways that are not good.
Fixing his eyes, he considers perverted things, and with his lips determines all evils; this man is a furnace of wickedness.
Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!

Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.
But in giving this instruction I do not praise you, because you come together for the worse rather than for the better.
For first, when you come together as a Church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I believe it in part.
For there must even be factions among you so that those who are approved may also become evident among you.
Therefore, when you gather in the same place, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper,
for in eating, each takes his own supper beforehand, and one is hungry while another is drunk.
Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise God’s Church and shame those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread,
and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord’s cup unworthily will be answerable for the Lord’s body and blood.
Besides becoming wise, Ecclesiastes also taught the people knowledge; and an ear will trace out an orderly arrangement of proverbs.
Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight and something written in uprightness, words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads and like planted nails, which were given from collections, from one shepherd, and something beyond them.
My son, beware of making many books; there is no limit, and much study is weariness of the flesh.

peer_precision_changes.rationale: Sirach connects proud quarrels with bloodshed and mutual abuse; Proverbs says a wrathful man digs up strife and an angry man digs out sins. Both connect quarrelsome behavior with further wrongdoing or harm.

Both expressly say that the person who digs a pit will fall into it. Sirach adds a setter caught in his own trap, extending the pattern of the action's adverse result returning on the actor. Ecclesiastes' surrounding examples also concern work hazards, so malicious intention is not assigned to its pit digger.

Sirach portrays those abandoning the Lord as prey of destructive speech, likened to a ravaging animal. The psalm joins a warning about a talkative man with evils hunting the unjust person to destruction.
Sirach commends the good man who stands surety for his neighbor. Judah's surety for Benjamin becomes an offer to remain enslaved in his place, a concrete instance of accepting another's liability.

Sirach commends standing surety for another; Paul offers to have any debt Onesimus may owe charged to himself and personally promises repayment. The letter supplies an explicit offer of financial guarantee.
Both ancient sayings connect love for a son with parental discipline. Proverbs contrasts this with sparing the staff; Sirach adds the father's hoped-for joy in later days.

Sirach withholds authority from a son in youth. Paul's illustration likewise places the child heir under guardians and stewards until the father's appointed time, despite the child's status as master of everything.

Sirach connects a bright, good heart with taking care over food; Ecclesiastes directs eating bread with gladness and drinking wine with a good heart. Both connect a good heart with the manner of eating.

Both combine references to strength with a warning about drinking. Sirach explicitly rejects proving one's manliness through wine; Isaiah pronounces woe on strong and powerful people who drink wine and mix strong drink.

Within Sirach 33:16-18 the late gleaner image describes gathering instruction for others. Ecclesiastes likewise describes a wise teacher teaching the people knowledge and seeking truthful written words; the agricultural image belongs only to Sirach.
Sirach says his labor serves everyone seeking instruction rather than himself alone. Ecclesiastes likewise describes the wise author teaching the people knowledge.
